## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.0`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noUnsafeUnaryMinus`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`types`](/linter/domains#types)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-unary-minus`](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/no-unsafe-unary-minus)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noUnsafeUnaryMinus": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require the operand of unary `-` to be a `number` or a `bigint`.

Unary negation converts any other operand to a number first. Negating a
string, boolean, nullish value, or object usually produces `NaN` or an
unexpected number, and TypeScript accepts many of these cases without
reporting an error.

Operands typed as `any` or `never` are allowed. Explicit `unknown`
operands are reported.

## Examples

### Invalid

```ts title='invalid-string.ts'
declare const value: string;
-value;
```

### Valid

```ts title='valid-number.ts'
declare const value: number;
-value;
```

```ts title='valid-numeric-union.ts'
declare const value: number | bigint;
-value;
```

```ts title='valid-member.ts'
declare const value: { x: number };
-value.x;
```
